p8_b0.ocr: The analysis of the data presented in Table 1 highlights significant findings related to the prevalence of large pulmonary embolism (PE) across different groups. Notably, the odds ratio (OR) for Group 3 indicates a substantial association with large PE, reported at 5.974 with a 95% confidence interval (CI) spanning from 1.811 to 19.703.

p8_b1.ocr: This suggests that individuals in this group are nearly six times more likely to experience large PE compared to the reference cohort, with a statistically significant P- value of .003, underscoring the robustness of this association. Furthermore, the mean value for this group is recorded at 836.60 ± 48.97, reflecting not only the central tendency but also the variability of the data.

p8_b5.ocr: The range of observed values from 776 to 934 provides additional context for the distribution of the measurements within Group 3.

p8_b6.ocr: These results emphasize the need for targeted clinical interventions and further research to understand the underlying mechanisms contributing to the increased risk of large PE in this population.
